findings.text: follow-on: held_trees is built only from _live_worktree_claims(), so the peer exemption applies only to worktrees a live run currently holds; an uncommitted file under the completing run's grant that sits in a terminal or reclaimed peer worktree is still charged to the completing run. This is the residual of the same defect outside the in-flight case the node names, and it should be recorded rather than silently accepted.

follow-on: _repository_scope_paths resolves a peer's declared path into a repository-relative root, and the exemption compares it against the repository-relative snapshot entries; a peer that declares an absolute path outside both its worktree and the repository is dropped by the helper, so a peer's file at such a path would stay charged. That matches how the completing run's own declaration is resolved, so the behaviour is consistent rather than a defect, but the boundary is worth a test.

follow-on: the new stray-edit case exercises only the unfenced full-scan path; the fenced boundary walk, whose roots are limited to the completing run's own worktree and the main checkout, never reaches a peer worktree, so the peer_grants lookup is dead on that path and the case does not cover it. The omission does not weaken this node's guard.
